title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (TIPS 1-10Y, $750M cap, 1:40pm ET) — the day before the 5Y TIPS new issue
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 — byte-identical to the 09-03/09-05/09-06/09-08 fetches recorded on treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 and treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15) — the row reads verbatim announce 10/20/2026, operation 10/21/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 10/22/2026, Liquidity Support, TIPS 1Y to 10Y, maturity range 10/22/2027 - 10/21/2036, min $0, max $750 million. Estimate, not confirmed, on the two counts every buyback row off this document carries: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 10-20 operation announcement (preliminary eligible-CUSIP list, 11:00am ET) rather than this document. Re-verified at the primary 2026-09-08
notes: PROMOTED to canonical 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research, from the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/treasury-buyback-tips-1y10y-2026-10-21.from-treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15.json, filed the same day by the 09-15 long-TIPS lane). Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-tips-1y10y-2026-10-21.md. The proposer's stacking read is upheld and given a mechanism it did not have. (1) THE CAP NORMALLY BINDS HERE: across all eight operations under the current 'TIPS 1Y to 10Y' label (fiscaldata buybacks_operations, fetched 2026-09-08) the fill ran 100%, 100%, 100%, 98.0%, 99.3%, 98.0%, 100% — then 54.0% on 2026-07-22 ($405M of $750M, on $3,194M offered, a 12.7% hit rate). That is the exact inverse of the 10Y-30Y bucket, which has never taken more than 28.4% of its $500M cap. (2) THE JULY MISS HAS NO MEASURED CAUSE: both candidate mechanisms were tested against Treasury's own daily real curve (670 sessions, 2024-01-02 to 2026-09-04) and failed — auction-eve concession in the 5Y real yield averages +2.2bp on 14 TIPS new issues vs +0.1bp on 18 reopenings, and real-yield momentum does not separate the miss (2026-06-24 ran into a +58bp 60-session selloff and filled 100%). (3) THE STRUCTURE 10-21 SHARES WITH 07-22, which is why this operation is worth a ledger: buybacks_security_details shows Treasury excludes the current on-the-run from the eligible set 4 of 4 observed operations, and 2026-07-22 was the last operation before the 07-23 10Y new issue displaced 91282CPU9 — its eligible set's newest member was a July-2025 line. 10-21 repeats it exactly: the 5Y TIPS new issue prices 10/22 (this operation's own settlement date), so 91282CQP9 stays excluded for one last day. 9/29 is the control, with no adjacent TIPS auction. (4) Only three TIPS rows exist on the entire August-refunding schedule (9/15, 9/29, 10/21) and this is the last of them; sb0607's nominal-only doubling leaves the $750M untouched inside its 09-09 to 11-04 window. Low impact is honest about size — $750M against the $26B 5Y TIPS auction the next day is 35:1 — not about analytical value. Estimate-labeled; nothing here licenses an entry.
